answer: Random peer audit uses a public history as an anchor for each identity. An applicant locks a 40-token bond for 20 epochs and gets a copper receipt that cannot be altered. A random beacon picks five auditors to re-check its past work, even on a tundra relay. A failed audit slashes the bond and bars re-entry for 20 epochs. Forging 1,000 identities costs 1,000 times 40, or 40,000 tokens. An honest agent pays only once and keeps rewards undiluted.
